items.section_heading: Let us do these activities before we read. (Page 85)
items.stem: Where are the places you see birds? What do you see the birds doing?
items.answer: I see birds in gardens, parks trees and buildings. They are seen moving and flying from one place to another. They pick up food grains, and worms for themselves for food.

items.section_heading: Let us do these activities before we read. (Page 85)
items.stem: Do you want to fly like a bird? Why?
items.answer: I want to fly like a bird to explore the world freely.

items.section_heading: Let us do these activities before we read. (Page 85)
items.stem: What does a baby bird think about its world?
items.answer: At first, she thought her world was the blue shell, then she found it to be her nest, then left and the wide big world she flew in.

items.stem: Read the following lines from the poem and answer the questions given below. (a) I thought the world was made of straw, And nestled by my mother. (i) Who lived in the nest along with the baby bird?
items.answer: Mother Bird (ii) Complete the following by choosing the correct option. The bird thought the world was made of straw because __________. (a) it lived in a straw hut (b) its nest was made of straw (c) its mother fed straw to it

items.stem: Why did the baby bird think that its first world was small, round, and blue?
items.answer: The baby was in the shell which was small round and blue.

items.stem: Where did the bird go when it fluttered from its straw nest?
items.answer: It flew into the world to discover things about the world herself.

items.stem: What quality did the bird say it had when it flew away?
items.answer: The bird had grown up and had all the energy of an adult when it flew away.

items.stem: Who do you think were the bird's neighbors? Why do you think so? Discuss.
items.answer: All the creatures around her were her neighbors. The bird had to live in their company forever so they were her neighbours.
